question: Can the known two-repetitions-per-class run design improve balanced decoding by combining hierarchy scores with unlabeled within-assigned-class event similarity?

implementation.assignment_solver: exact enumeration of all 2,520 assignments with two events per class
implementation.similarity_feature: full native offset-3 length-8 mean map after subject-run centering and linear event-time detrending
implementation.selection_protocol: consistency weight chosen by four inner subject folds independently for every outer fold

acceptance_criteria: Lambda zero must exactly reconstruct every stored balanced outer-fold result.
A nonzero weight must be selected using outer-training subjects only.
Repeated outer-fold and subject-level paired bootstrap intervals must exclude zero before promotion.
Independent decoding must remain separately reported because this layer requires known complete-run composition.

decision.interpretation: Nested repetition consistency gives a repeatable 1.42-point balanced gain with positive fold and subject intervals. It improves both leg and arm recalls and is not driven by excluding failed subjects. Use 0.8948 as the strongest zero-label complete-run balanced result and retain 0.8314 from the temporal candidate selector for independent or unbalanced deployment.
